alt_title_2: Stop Doing $5 Robot Chores With Your Brain
description_hook: A 2012 McKinsey report estimated knowledge workers spend about 28% of the workweek on email. Use the 3x Automation Rule to remove 3 repetitive chores for good.

scenes.headline: You Are Acting Like a Human Router
scenes.stat_label: OF THE WORKWEEK SPENT ON EMAIL
bullets: McKinsey (2012): ~28% of the workweek goes to email
Copying data across tabs drains deep creative focus
scenes.narration: A 2012 McKinsey report estimated that knowledge workers spend about twenty-eight percent of their workweek just reading and answering email.

scenes.headline: The Engineer's 3-Strike Automation Rule
scenes.stat_label: REPEAT IT THREE TIMES -> AUTOMATE IT ONCE
bullets: 1st time: Do it manually to learn the steps
3rd time in a week: Build a permanent AI or webhook flow
scenes.narration: Programmers have a rule of three: the third time you repeat something, automate it. Apply it to your week. If you do the same digital task three times, stop and automate it.
scenes.source: 'Rule of three', popularized in Martin Fowler, Refactoring (1999)

scenes.headline: 3 Chores to Hand Off Immediately
scenes.left_body: 1. Typing call notes  2. Sorting PDF receipts  3. Reformatting posts
scenes.right_body: AI call summaries -> auto-tagged cloud folders -> 1-click drafts
scenes.narration: Start with three culprits: typing meeting action items, renaming email receipts for taxes, and reformatting one script into social posts. Modern AI workflows handle all three in seconds.

scenes.headline: 15 Minutes Saved Daily = 91 Hours a Year
scenes.stat_subtext: Reinvest those 91 hours into high-margin skills and assets
scenes.narration: Cut fifteen minutes of daily busywork and you get back about ninety-one hours a year for real work.

scenes.headline: Protect Your Brain for Asymmetric Work
bullets: Robots never forget a step at 4 PM on Friday
Save human energy for judgment and strategy
scenes.narration: Let software do the robot work so your brain stays sharp for high-value judgment.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
